scope: Exact Chromium source audit; this is not a renderer or binary acceptance test
notes: Google's dynamic CRLSet and root-store updates are separate from this compiled blocklist.
A missing entry does not establish that every default-root chain is accepted; it means static SPKI distrust is unproven, including alternate or explicitly trusted chains.
CEF's asynchronous CefLoadCRLSetsFile call has no completion callback. Calling it before creating a browser does not establish first-request protection.
Renderer acceptance must distinguish ERR_CERT_REVOKED from untrusted, expired, hostname, connection, and Certificate Transparency failures, and include a valid control.

runtimeObservation.scope: Standalone application linked against the downloaded CEF156 library; not Electrobun release acceptance
runtimeObservation.navigation: about:blank loaded before component registration completed
runtimeObservation.conclusion: CEF156 provides Chromium component updates, but a fresh profile does not start with the incident revocations installed.

startupOrdering.finding: CefLoadCRLSetsFile starts asynchronous file loading and supplies DoNothing as the verifier update completion callback.
UpdateCRLSet schedules another asynchronous parse; callback fires after parse and verifier updates, including malformed or obsolete inputs. UI task ordering alone cannot establish readiness.
The CRLSet component installer also starts asynchronous reading and supplies DoNothing on verifier update.
ComponentReady and component-install completion are separate notifications. UPDATED state or an update callback does not confirm verifier policy application.
CRLSet checking is skipped when a certificate path is already invalid; an unrelated self-signed or incomplete chain cannot prove compromised-key revocation.

recommendedRemediation.preferred: Compile the eight compromised SPKIs into Chromium cert_verify_proc_blocklist.inc in the distributed CEF binaries. This applies from first verification and survives later CRLSet replacement.
recommendedRemediation.alternative: Expose successful verifier application through CEF, distribute a complete authenticated CRLSet containing the keys, and gate application networking until confirmed policy application, including network-service restarts.
avoid: Treating component update completion as verifier readiness
Treating any TLS failure as compromised-key rejection
Replacing a complete CRLSet with only eight keys and an artificially high sequence

verificationStillRequired: Real renderer acceptance that rejects an otherwise trusted compromised-key chain specifically as ERR_CERT_REVOKED and accepts an unrelated valid chain
First request on an empty profile and after network-service restart
